evidence: src/application/AdvanceOrderUseCase.ts: validateExecute(status: unknown) { if (!isOrderStatus(status)) throw new DomainError("invalid", "Unknown order state"); }. It is never called from execute(orderId).
src/application/ListOrdersByStatusUseCase.ts: execute(status: unknown) runs the same check: if (!isOrderStatus(status)) throw new DomainError("invalid", "Unknown order state").

src/application/AdvanceOrderUseCase.ts and src/application/CancelOrderUseCase.ts both repeat: const order = await this.orders.findById(orderId); if (!order) throw new DomainError("not_found", `Order ${orderId} not found`).
All use cases consistently use dto.ts mappers (toOrderDto, toStockLevelDto) and domain repositories, so the overall concern is cohesive.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module is mostly one coherent unit: order and stock use cases that share the DTO mappers in dto.ts (toOrderDto, toStockLevelDto) and the domain repositories. One rule is written in two places, though. AdvanceOrderUseCase has a public method, validateExecute(status: unknown), that repeats exactly the status check in ListOrdersByStatusUseCase.execute, including the same error message: `if (!isOrderStatus(status)) throw new DomainError("invalid", "Unknown order state")`. The method also has nothing to do with its own use case. AdvanceOrderUseCase.execute takes an orderId, not a status, and never calls validateExecute. So the check is a stray second copy that could drift from the first. The "order not found" check is also repeated, in AdvanceOrderUseCase.execute and CancelOrderUseCase.execute, but that is a smaller issue. Because of the duplicated status rule, the unit fails.
